advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make a bare `--limit` (and `--limit` followed by a dash-prefixed token) fail with 'Error: --limit requires a value', the way `--only` does
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:340: if arg in _VALUE_FLAGS and i + 1 < len(argv) and not argv[i + 1].startswith("-"):
src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:378-379: for a in argv: / if a.startswith("--limit="):  — a bare '--limit' never matches, so limit stays None
src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:393: fmt, _rest = parse_output(argv, "report")  — leftover '--limit' and '-5' tokens end up in _rest and are never checked
src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:359-361: '--only' gets an explicit 'requires a value' error; '--limit' has no matching check
src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:314-315: _fsck_govern only adds --limit to its argv when limit is not None, so the argparse check never sees the bare flag
advisory.finding: A bare `--limit` (last on the command line, or followed by another flag) and a negative `--limit -N` are not folded. They are then silently ignored, so limit stays None and `--repair` runs over every ticket. `--only` gets an explicit 'requires a value' error in the same situation, so the two flags this change claims to treat alike still behave differently.
scenarios: `rebar store fsck --repair --limit --dry-run` runs with no limit instead of failing
`rebar store fsck --repair --limit -5` drops the limit, while `--limit=-5` parses to -5
advisory.suggested_fix: After `argv = _join_flag_values(argv)`, add: `if "--limit" in argv: sys.stderr.write("Error: --limit requires a value\n"); return 2`. Add tests for `["--repair", "--limit"]` and `["--limit", "--repair"]`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider checking that the space spelling gets past validation through observable output (e.g. a tmp_path repo_root with no tracker, then assert rc==1 and the NOT_INITIALIZED error) instead of patching the private _fsck_govern
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:298: "Return the rejection render code, or ``None`` when dispatch may continue."
src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:409-410: if _rc is not None: return _rc  (the stub's 0 short-circuits here, so `fsck_cli(argv) == 0` reflects the stub)
advisory.finding: test_accepted_spellings_reach_dispatch_with_the_same_values monkeypatches the private helper `fsck._fsck_govern`, which is internal to fsck_cli. The test is therefore tied to that internal seam: it breaks if the helper is renamed or inlined, even though behavior is unchanged. The stub also returns 0, while the real helper returns None to mean 'continue', so the test's rc==0 is an artifact of the stub and not of real dispatch.
scenarios: A refactor that inlines or renames _fsck_govern without changing CLI behavior makes this test fail.

evidence: src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:330-331: "Fold ``--only <value>`` / ``--limit <value>`` into the ``=`` form so both spellings parse the same."
tests/unit/test_fsck_only_flag.py:78: `["--repair", "--only", "stale-channel", "--limit", "3"]` checks that --limit's space spelling reaches dispatch

advisory.finding: The space-to-equals fold also applies to --limit, which the ticket does not ask for. Its title, ACs and file_impact cover only --only ("`--only <value>` (space-separated) and `--only=<value>` behave the same"). This changes how --limit is parsed, and no acceptance criterion states it.
scenarios: An operator or later reviewer reads the ticket ACs and does not expect `rebar store fsck --limit 3` to change behaviour in this change
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a line to ticket e395-114c-aee9-42a5 such as '`--limit <N>` and `--limit=<N>` behave the same' (and add fsck.py's --limit handling to file_impact) so the ACs match what ships, or split the --limit fold into a separate ticket.
